Most campus plugins have three layers: an HTTP call, a parser, and a tool that shapes the result.
Cover the parser and the shaping with `bun test`, then try the whole thing in the app.

## Plugin documents (PLUGIN.md)

You test a `PLUGIN.md` plugin with the author CLI in the plugins repository. It replays the
recorded responses in the plugin's `tests/*.yaml`:

```bash
bun run plugin validate plugins/classrooms   # the checks the app runs
bun run plugin test plugins/classrooms       # replay tests/*.yaml
bun run plugin run plugins/classrooms overview '{}'   # live, public hosts only
```

`bun test` includes `plugins/documents.test.ts`, which loads every `plugins/<id>/PLUGIN.md` and
replays all its recorded tests, so CI fails as soon as a document or its fixtures break. The test
format is described in the [quickstart](/en/docs/build/quickstart#record-a-test). The rest of this
page covers TypeScript plugins.

## Unit tests (bun test)

Run these in the plugins repository:

```bash
bun test                      # every *.test.ts in the workspace
bun test plugins/focus        # one plugin
bunx tsc --noEmit -p .        # typecheck SDK + plugins
```

(`focus` is the example plugin from [Bundled plugin](/en/docs/build/bundled-plugin); use your own
plugin's folder.)

- Put tests next to the code: `src/parse.test.ts` beside `src/parse.ts`.
- **Parsers**: save real responses as fixtures (`src/fixtures/*.html|json`) with personal data
  replaced, and assert on the parsed result. Campus pages change, and a fixture shows exactly what
  broke.
- **Time**: pass `now` in explicitly instead of reading `Date.now()` inside logic. The SDK's
  recurrence, timetable and format helpers all take `now`.
- **React Native**: modules that import `react-native` won't load under bun unless you mock it.
  Keep logic in plain modules, or mock it the way `plugins/i18n.test.ts` does:

```ts
import { mock } from 'bun:test';

mock.module('react-native', () => ({
  StyleSheet: { create: (s: unknown) => s },
  Platform: { OS: 'android', select: (o: Record<string, unknown>) => o.android ?? o.default },
  View: () => null,
}));
```

### Testing a tool with a fake context

```ts title="plugins/focus/src/index.test.ts"
import { expect, mock, test } from 'bun:test';
import type { KV, ToolContext } from '@pku-harness/sdk';

// index.ts imports the widget, which imports react-native: mock it before loading the plugin.
mock.module('react-native', () => ({ View: () => null }));
const { focusPlugin } = await import('./index');

function memoryKV(): KV {
  const m = new Map<string, unknown>();
  return {
    get: async <T,>(k: string) => m.get(k) as T | undefined,
    set: async (k, v) => void m.set(k, v),
    delete: async (k) => void m.delete(k),
  };
}

test('start, then today shows the running session', async () => {
  const ctx = { pluginId: 'focus', actor: 'user', kv: memoryKV(), services: {} } as unknown as ToolContext;
  await focusPlugin.tools.start.execute({ label: '高数' }, ctx);
  const today = (await focusPlugin.tools.today.execute({}, ctx)) as { running: { label: string } | null };
  expect(today.running?.label).toBe('高数');
});
```

`execute` doesn't validate its input; the host does that. If validation matters, test it separately
with `tool.input.safeParse(...)`.

## Mock model

`examples/mock-llm` is a scripted OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions server. It lets you exercise
the agent loop without an API key:

```bash
bun examples/mock-llm/server.ts     # http://localhost:8788/v1, model "mock-agent"
```

In the app, go to Settings → AI service → OpenAI-compatible and set the base URL to
`http://10.0.2.2:8788/v1` (from the emulator) and the model to `mock-agent`. It picks a tool based
on keywords in your message, then summarises the tool result:

| Message contains | It calls |
| --- | --- |
| `提醒` / `remind` | `scheduler__create` (every 3 days at 09:00, 16 times) |
| `马上` / `soon` | `scheduler__create` (once, in 2 minutes) |
| `看板` / `dash` | `dashboard__upsertWidget` (a widget bound to `timetable.today`) |
| `表单` / `form` | `ui__render` (a top-up form) |
| `remember` | `memory__remember` |
| `食堂` / `canteen` | `mcp-demo-canteen__reserveSeat` (needs the demo plugin installed) |
| `who` | Echoes the injected `<context>` block |

To call your own tools, extend its `plan()` function locally with their model names.

## Demo remote plugin

```bash
bun examples/demo-canteen/server.ts   # :8787/mcp, bearer token demo-token
```

In Settings → Plugins → Add remote plugin, add `http://10.0.2.2:8787/mcp` with token `demo-token`.
It has one read tool (`menu`) and one write tool (`reserveSeat`), so you get to see the approval
prompt for remote writes.

## On a device

- Dev-only deep links run a tool or a chat turn:
  `pkuharness://dev?tool=<plugin>.<tool>&input=<json>` and `pkuharness://dev?chat=<text>`.
  Add `&actor=agent` to trigger the ask-first prompts.
- Check screens and widgets in both themes (dark and light) and both languages.
- Real campus data needs a real account. Test read tools on your own account before asking anyone
  else to, and never commit responses that contain personal data.
